addenda.title: The patio doors: their glass and their width
items: Item 1 (data): the patio doors (D1) are glazed with tempered glass (IBC 2018 2406.4.1).
Item 2 (size): the patio doors narrow from 6'-0" to 5'-0" wide, centred where they were.

addenda.title: The rooms, the plumbing walls and the service annex
items: 1. Every room as a space (IfcSpace), 122 in all: its use, the openings in its walls and its net floor area, from forge `rooms` (pass 3g step 1).
2. The flats' walls: 72 partitions and 12 plumbing walls (IFC's PLUMBINGWALL), each plumbing wall 1/2 in. clear of the party wall.
3. The service annex behind the stair: its walls, slab and roof; a mechanical and plumbing room (door D5) and an electrical room (door D4), each with its own outside door.
4. The ground floor's back stair window removed (1-stair/back/0 was safety glazed): the annex covers it. Safety glazing goes 14 -> 13 openings.

5. Each bedroom's escape window named (24): its own type (W3), side-hinged (a casement), since hung or sliding a window of their size can't clear IBC 2021 1031; every window now says whether it is one (Pset_WindowCommon.FireExit).

addenda.title: The envelope to Pennsylvania's 2021 energy code
items: Item 1 (walls): the exterior walls, and the service annex's, take R-3.8 continuous insulation (1 in. of board outboard of the sheathing) over the R-20 cavities: U-0.051, the 2021 IECC's (Table R402.1.3, 20 + 3.8). The walls thicken inward from 7 to 8 in.; the building's outside stays 100 x 40 ft, so the rooms along the outside walls lose 1 in. and the stair, set against the back wall, moves with it.
Item 2 (slabs): the ground floor's heated slab sits on R-5 under its full area, with R-10 at its edge to 4 ft; the annex's slab takes the same edge insulation (Table R402.1.3 and its footnote d).
The windows (U-0.30) and the roof (R-49) already meet the 2021 code: no change.
